title: Exposure-time distribution as a product-purity coordinate
abstract: A synthetic historical object that interprets target-only and multi-edit products as potentially requiring different exposure times while retaining the absence of a practical control mechanism.
disposition_reason: The kinetic coordinate remained plausible but lacked a selective mitochondrial actuator.
nearest_prior_art: General exposure-time control in catalytic systems.
strongest_reason: Different product classes can have separable dwell-time requirements.
weakest_causal_edge: No practical intervention was shown to selectively shorten the relevant exposure distribution.
pairwise_summary: No pairwise comparison occurred in this child run.
reviewer_disagreement: Reviewers differed on whether exposure could be controlled independently of burden.
reviewer_critiques: A global activity reduction would not distinguish the proposed kinetic mechanism.
reentry_condition: Re-enter only with an actuator that changes exposure without proportionally changing all products.
scientific_summary: Target-only and multi-edit products may occupy different parts of an exposure-time distribution.
causal_mechanism: Shorter effective exposure could preserve early desired products before later bystander events accumulate.
evidence_basis: Synthetic kinetic interpretation without a validated mitochondrial control mechanism.
next_discriminating_experiment: Compare matched interventions that alter exposure timing and test whether all product classes change proportionally.
